conviction_note: The event is confirmed: per the company IR release, monday.com reports Q3 2026 on Mon 9 Nov, with the call at 08:30 ET. The evidence points both ways. Peers that reported after monday.com last spoke were sold hard: Atlassian fell 14.6% on 6 Nov, HubSpot fell 5.4% on 5 Nov on a flat Q4 guide, and Freshworks fell 6.3% on 4 Nov. Against that, monday.com has beaten the top of its own revenue guide by about $9-12M two quarters running, management said in August that it held back the Q2 upside because of restructuring risk, the sell-side downgraded steadily into the print, and 16.6% of the float is short. The per-finding sum (+0.8) and the scaled number (-0.9) differ in sign because the sum gives the beat, the possible raise and the positioning their own small sizes. p_up of 47 reflects the name's record: on three of its last four confirmed prints it fell 5-21% on the guide, including after beats.
bar: Revenue. Company Q3 guide $368-370M (+16-17% y/y), FY26 guide $1,466-1,474M, Q3 non-GAAP operating income $57-59M (Q2 2026 release, https://s29.q4cdn.com/881027206/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-26-PR-monday-com-August-2026.pdf, 2026-08-10). Street: Q3 revenue $376.75M and EPS $1.40 from 26 analysts (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/mndy/earnings, read 2026-11-06); FY26 revenue $1.47B and EPS $5.50, FY27 $1.69B (+15%) (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mndy/forecast/, read 2026-11-06). The two Street sources do not agree with each other: a $376.75M Q3 plus a $1.47B FY would imply Q4 below Q3. So the Street bar for the quarter and the implied Q4 is disputed, and the guidance-dependent findings are capped small. The company guide is the only bar sourced to a primary document. My read is a Q3 near $378-380M, which is about +0.6% against $376.75M and about +2.7% against the guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest is 16.58% of float with a short ratio of 4.38 days (Finviz quote page, read 2026-11-06, https://finviz.com/quote.ashx?t=MNDY; settlement date not shown). Other undated aggregators give 17.1-21.9%. Skew (25-delta put IV minus call IV) is +2.86 vol points, a mild bid for puts. Put/call open interest is 1.57. The event-implied move is 17.73%, with ATM IV at 126%. The sell-side downgraded into the print: Cantor, Capital One and Wolfe in August; JPMorgan on 29 Sep (to Neutral, $87); Barclays on 12 Oct (to Equal Weight, $100); Zacks on 15 Oct; Piper reiterated Neutral ($90) on 29 Oct; TD Cowen on 3 Nov (to Hold, $105). Ratings now stand at 12 Buy and 13 Hold (MarketBeat, 2026-11-03). Spot is $92.02: down 51% from the 52-week high, up 17% from the 29 Sep low of $76, and down 14% from the 22 Oct high of $106.86. Realised vol is 61%, and 15 of 37 sessions in Sep-Oct moved more than 4%. The short is moderately crowded, which argues for shrinking the negatives.

findings.finding: Peers that reported after monday.com's 10 Aug call were sold on decelerating guides even when they beat. HubSpot (SMB-focused, seat-based) guided Q4 revenue to $945-947M, +12% y/y and flat on Q3's $947.6M (+17%), and its release cited 'changes in customer buying behavior for AI solutions'; HUBS fell from $216.64 to $204.96 (-5.4%) on 5 Nov. Atlassian beat (revenue +24%) but guided FY27 subscription ARR to about 18.5% from 23%; TEAM fell from $183.29 to $156.57 (-14.6%) on 6 Nov. Freshworks fell from $14.15 to $13.26 (-6.3%) on 4 Nov. monday.com's own implied Q4 is already about +16% y/y, and the market is treating any seat-based deceleration harshly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On guidance, monday.com fell 12.3% on 10 Nov 2025 (Q4 guide), 20.8% on 9 Feb 2026 (FY26 guide of 19-20%) and 4.8% on 10 Aug 2026 (Q3 guide below consensus, despite a beat). It rose 6.7% close to close on 11 May 2026 when it raised the FY guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Only partly priced. MNDY fell 14% from 22 Oct to 6 Nov and 2.6% on the day Atlassian fell 14.6%, while IGV fell about 11% over the same stretch. MNDY absorbed about a sixth of TEAM's single-day move. If the read-through were fully priced, MNDY would have tracked the peer drops more closely and the skew would be steeper than +2.86.
findings.independence: Separate documents from separate companies. Atlassian coverage: https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/atlassian-tumbles-16-on-weaker-subscription-growth-outlook-5005613 (2026-11-06). Price series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/TEAM?range=1mo&interval=1d and https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/FRSH?range=1mo&interval=1d. These are peer proxies; monday.com has not confirmed any of it.

findings.finding: monday.com beat the top of its own revenue guide in both 2026 quarters. Q1 came in at $351.3M against a $338-340M guide (+$11M). Q2 came in at $364.6M against a $355.5M consensus that sat at the guide (+$9M). The same pattern on a $368-370M Q3 guide points to about $377-381M, which is only marginally above the $376.75M Street figure.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: monday.com sells its beats. Q2 2026 beat by about 2.6% and the stock fell 4.8%. The Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 beats were followed by drops of 12.3% and 20.8% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. The Street's $376.75M is already about $7M above the top of the guide, so the buy-side expects the usual beat. Only a beat well above $380M would surprise.
findings.independence: The Q2 beat comes from a separate document, the Q2 release (https://s29.q4cdn.com/881027206/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/Q2-26-PR-monday-com-August-2026.pdf, 2026-08-10), and the consensus figure from https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/mondaycom-fallt-nach-schwacherer-q3-umsatzprognose-aktie-10-und-ytd-42.

findings.finding: In August the CFO kept the FY26 guide at $1,466-1,474M despite the Q2 beat, explicitly because the effect of the 20% workforce cut was unknown: 'we prefer to underpromise and overdeliver through a transition'. The implied Q4 at the midpoint is about $385M (+16% y/y). Q3 is the first full quarter since the restructuring. If the Q3 beat (about $8-10M) flows through, FY rises to about $1.478B, above the $1.47B FY consensus. If FY is only held, implied Q4 drops to about $376M, flat on Q3, which is the HubSpot shape the market just punished.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: monday.com rose 6.7% on the May 2026 FY raise (a third-party source says it rose 20.9% intraday) and fell 4.8% in August 2026 when the FY guide was held.
findings.why_not_priced: The FY consensus ($1.47B, stockanalysis/S&P) sits at the guide midpoint, so the Street has not modelled the Q2 upside being released. If it had, FY consensus would read about $1.475-1.48B. The bar is disputed (see bar), so the finding is capped small.
findings.independence: Same company and the same quarter's documents as the Q2 release. The 'restructuring uncertainty' framing is corroborated by the Panabee and Yahoo coverage of the Q2 call; no independent company source confirms a raise.

findings.finding: The CFO guided FY26 net dollar retention to 108% (Q2 was 109%), with 'modest pressure on NDR in the back half as prior pricing actions are lapped'; tier upgrades and multi-product expansion were 'slightly below our original expectations'. A Q3 NDR of about 108% would land inside what was guided.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history on NDR alone; it is reported alongside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced because it was guided. Only an NDR print of 107% or below would be news.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the previous finding; the Q2 NDR of 109% comes from the Q2 release.

findings.finding: Expectations were reset ahead of the print. Eight rating cuts or neutral reiterations since August took the count to 12 Buy and 13 Hold, with price targets of $87-105 against a $92 spot. 16.58% of the float is short, with a short ratio of 4.38. Adequate Q4 guidance would face a washed-out holder base and a moderately crowded short.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 37% from the 29 Sep low ($76.05, the day of the JPMorgan downgrade) to 22 Oct ($106.86) with no company news, so it does squeeze. In Sep-Oct 15 of 37 sessions moved more than 4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price. What is not priced is how a 16-17% short base reacts to a guide that clears a lowered bar. If that were priced, the skew would be flat or call-bid; at +2.86 it is mildly put-bid.
findings.independence: Downgrade list from a separate source: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-mondaycom-nasdaq-mndy-stock-rating-cut-to-hold-at-td-cowen-2026-11-03/ (2026-11-03).

findings.finding: TD Cowen's downgrade to Hold on 3 Nov ($110 to $105) argues that about 40% of ARR is downmarket. That segment is exposed to AI-driven erosion of search, SEO and SEM customer acquisition. TD Cowen sees 2026 as less risky and expects more pressure in 2027, which puts the risk on any 2027 commentary on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Earlier top-of-funnel and search-erosion scares (BofA's downgrade on Google AI Overviews, the Aug 2025 print) produced large drops.
findings.why_not_priced: It is wire copy, so it is mostly priced; the stock has fallen about 3% since. The unpriced part is whether management gives early 2027 colour that confirms it.
findings.independence: On the Q2 call the CFO said the guide assumes no rebound in performance marketing or top-of-funnel activity (fool.com transcript), and Barclays cited AI at about 1% of ARR (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/mondaycom-aktie-barclays-stuft-auf-equal-weight-ab-ki-umsatz-bleibt-gering).

findings.finding: The $870M buyback authorization was fully used by the end of Q2: 2.33M shares were bought for $182M in Q2, and $735M was spent in H1. Cash and marketable securities total about $1.07B ($853.4M plus $219.4M) on a market cap of about $4.0B, and the stock is 51% below its high. No new authorization has been announced. A new one with the Q3 release would be a capital-return positive, but no source says one is coming.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated; past buybacks were announced alongside prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is an inference with a low probability-weighted size. If the market expected a new program, the put skew would be flatter and the stock would not have given back 14% in two weeks.

findings.finding: AI product ARR doubled from Q1 to Q2 and made up 17% of Q2 net new ARR, per the Q2 release. Barclays puts it at only about 1% of total ARR. Another doubling would support the AI-credits narrative, but in absolute terms it is too small to move revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The AI metric was disclosed with a beat in Q2, and the stock still fell 4.8% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, since the 1% share is in the downgrade copy. Only an AI ARR disclosure well above the doubling trend would be news.

outside_window.finding: The FY2027 guide, which TD Cowen expects to be under more pressure, normally comes with the Q4 print in February. Only early colour can land in this window.

baseline_tension: The peer evidence agrees with the mild put skew. The sell-side reset and the 16.6% short cut against it, as does the 20-day run-up of +3.4% (the stock is up from the Sep low but down 3.7% over five days). Net, the evidence is close to balanced against an implied move of 17.7%.

Lesson 6 (the Street bar is disputed): the guidance-raise finding was capped from +1.0 to +0.7, p_up moved from 46 to 47 toward 50, and print_vs_bar was re-measured explicitly against the $376.75M consensus (+0.6 instead of +1.0).
Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the NDR finding was moved toward 0, from -0.3 to -0.1.
